analysis.evidence: עֹד כָּל יְמֵי הָאָרֶץ means “as long as the earth endures.” It sets the duration of the promise that seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, and day and night will continue. לֹא negates יִשְׁבֹּתוּ (“they will cease”).
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb, defectively spelled עֹד, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָּל יְמֵי הָאָרֶץ means ‘all the days of the earth.’ כָּל takes the days together as the full span during which the cycles named in the verse will continue.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָּל־יְמֵי הָאָרֶץ means “all the days of the earth.” The phrase gives the duration of the promise that the cycles listed in the verse will continue for as long as the earth endures.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural construct, with הָאָרֶץ as its complement.
analysis.sense: (pl.) days of a life, a reign or an age

analysis.evidence: כָּל יְמֵי הָאָרֶץ means “all the days of the earth.” The promise that seedtime and harvest, summer and winter, and day and night will continue for that span refers to the earth as a whole.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + common noun, singular absolute, of common gender.

analysis.evidence: The verse pairs זֶרַע with קָצִיר, ‘harvest’. Like summer and winter or day and night, seedtime and harvest are recurring periods that the verse says will continue.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: זֶרַע וְקָצִיר pairs seedtime with harvest time. The parallel pairs of summer and winter and of day and night place harvest within the recurring cycles that לֹא יִשְׁבֹּתוּ says will continue.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

draft.change: Add קֹר under קרר with the weather sense shown in Genesis 8:22.
draft.definition: Cold as a condition of the weather.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 8:22, cold and heat form a pair of recurring conditions that will continue as long as the earth endures.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 8:22 pairs קֹר with חֹם, “heat,” just as it pairs summer with winter and day with night. The opposition to heat identifies קֹר as cold weather.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 8:22, וְקֹר וָחֹם means “cold and heat.” The pairing with קֹר identifies חֹם as heat in the recurring temperature cycle, alongside summer and winter and day and night.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: וְקַיִץ וָחֹרֶף pairs summer with winter, just as the verse pairs cold with heat and day with night. The seasonal contrast identifies the sense as summer.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: וְקַיִץ וָחֹרֶף pairs summer with winter, alongside the recurring contrasts of cold and heat and of day and night.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with prefixed conjunction וָ־.

analysis.evidence: The verse pairs וְיוֹם with וָלַיְלָה, “and day and night,” so יוֹם denotes the daylight portion of the cycle.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: daylight, the day as against night

analysis.evidence: In לֹא יִשְׁבֹּתוּ, “they will not cease,” לֹא negates the following verb. The clause affirms that the listed cycles will continue as long as the earth endures.
analysis.morphology: Negative particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The plural verb takes the paired subjects seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, and day and night. לֹא יִשְׁבֹּתוּ says that these cycles will continue for all the days of the earth.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine plural
